study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier provided in the paper.

target_condition.evidence_quote: characterized the gut microbiome of the Yanomami from Brazil
target_condition.notes: Primary focus is characterization of gut microbiome composition and functional diversity in traditional groups.

control.notes: Study compares traditional groups with urban group (US), but individual case/control status not assigned per participant.

country.evidence_quote: Yanomami from Brazil and compared taxonomically and functionally with the Yanomami from Venezuela
country.notes: Primary samples from Brazil; comparison samples from Venezuela, Peru, and United States also analyzed.

body_site.evidence_quote: Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample

body_site_details.notes: No specific anatomical subsite reported beyond fecal sample.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: The Yanomami is the largest indigenous semi-isolated group in the Amazon to maintain traditional subsistence

location.evidence_quote: They inhabit the Amazon region encompassing the Brazil and Venezuela border

westernized.evidence_quote: Human groups that still maintain traditional modes of subsistence (hunter–gatherers)
westernized.notes: Yanomami participants classified as traditional, non-westernized.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Escherichia and Ralstonia genera in the Yanomami/Brazil, Neisseria and Desulfovibrio were defined as Yanomami/Venezuela biomarkers, Cutibacterium and Akkermansia were biomarkers of the Yanomami/Brazil, Treponema and Brachyspira present in all traditional groups, regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, and virulence in Yanomami/Brazil.
biomarker_name.section: Results — Microbiomes Taxonomic Characterization; Results — Microbiomes Functional Characterization
biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers identified through LDA analysis and functional characterization at different taxonomic and functional levels. Multiple biomarkers reported for different groups and functional categories.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: LDA score of >4.0 were used as thresholds. relative abundance (percentage) of the most frequent phyla.
biomarker_unit.section: Materials and Methods — Bioinformatics Processing; Results — Microbiomes Taxonomic Characterization
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type: taxonomic biomarkers use relative abundance percentages and LDA scores; functional biomarkers use percentage abundance.

value: higher abundance (Escherichia and Ralstonia in Yanomami/Brazil)
higher abundance (regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, virulence in Yanomami/Brazil, P < 0.05)
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: LDA score of >4.0 were used as thresholds. Methanobrevibacter, comprising ∼70% of all archaea classified reads. higher abundance of Escherichia and Ralstonia. significantly higher abundance (P < 0.05) of gene families involved in regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, and virulence.

disease_response_os.notes: This study focuses on gut microbiome characterization in a traditional human population and does not report overall survival or disease outcomes.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable to this microbiome study.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Shannon index of alpha-diversity was estimated for each metagenome. Beta-diversity was determined using Bray–Curtis dissimilarity. relative abundance of the bacterial genera identified in each Yanomami/Brazil gut microbiome.
feces_phenotype_value.section: Materials and Methods — Statistical Analysis; Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal samples analyzed for microbiome composition and diversity. Multiple phenotypic measurements reported including taxonomic composition and functional potential.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this is a microbiome study in a traditional population without oncology endpoints.

value: Study participants: Yanomami from Brazil (n=15), Yanomami from Venezuela (n=8), Matses (n=24), Tunapuco (n=12), US urban population (n=44)
Sample type: stool/fecal samples, single sample per subject collected on morning after request
Sequencing platform: Illumina HiSeq 2500; ~219 million reads total, ~14 million reads per sample average
Bioinformatics tools: Kraken for taxonomic classification, LEfSe for biomarker identification (LDA score >4.0), SUPER-FOCUS for functional classification
Alpha-diversity: Yanomami showed lowest bacterial alpha-diversity among traditional groups; all traditional groups had higher diversity than urban group
Beta-diversity: Yanomami presented highest interpersonal variation; urban group presented lowest variation
Phyla identified: 32 bacterial phyla; 16 with significant differences among groups (Kruskal-Wallis P<0.0001)
Archaea: Methanobrevibacter ~70% in traditional groups; Methanoculleus and Methanothermobacter abundant in urban group
Functional differences: Traditional groups enriched in central carbohydrate metabolism; urban group enriched in membrane transport (P<2e-05)
Yanomami/Brazil unique features: higher abundance of regulation/cell signaling, motility/chemotaxis, and virulence gene families (P<0.05)
Virulence in Yanomami/Brazil driven by cobalt, zinc, and cadmium resistance genes
Ethics approval: Oswaldo Cruz Foundation's Ethics Research Committee No. 638/11; CONEP No. 16907
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 15 stool samples from Yanomami/Brazil, 8 from Yanomami/Venezuela, 24 Matses, 12 Tunapuco, 44 US individuals. ~219 million reads total, ~14 million reads per sample. Kraken for taxonomic classification, LEfSe with LDA score >4.0 threshold, SUPER-FOCUS for functional classification.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive study design and methodology details provided for reproducibility and contextual understanding of findings.

host_species.evidence_quote: Yanomami is the largest semi-nomadic hunter–gatherer group of the Americas, semi-isolated Yanomami individuals from Brazil, indigenous representatives, Yanomami individuals showed the lowest bacterial alpha-diversity among the traditional groups
host_species.notes: Host species inferred from study context describing human populations (Yanomami, Matses, Tunapuco, US individuals). No explicit species designation provided but clearly human based on context.
